cards.title: The Mob: four peasants
cards.text: Torch, pitchfork, axe, dagger: four small peasants, one hero. Three sets. Mine: the village.
cards.why: You wrote: "Mob. Is 4 peasants... Torch, pitchfork, axe, and dagger." Each is about 60% of a hero, with the heroes' line weight. I'd take the village: four colours and four head shapes, so they stay four people at game size. The game keeps its stand-in until you pick.

items.label: A the village
items.text: A red kerchief (torch), a slouched felt hat (pitchfork), a bald woodcutter with a black beard (axe), an ochre pointed hood (dagger).

items.label: B the kitchen militia
items.text: The same sackcloth on all four; a colander, a bucket, a cooking pot and a funnel for helmets.

items.label: C one family
items.text: Grandmother, father, big son and child, four sizes. The child is very small on a phone.

items.label: All three, side by side
items.text: Not one to pick: the three takes together at game scale beside the archer, and at game size in four facings.

items.label: In a row with five heroes
items.text: Not one to pick: each take standing third in a row of six with five heroes you approved, big and at game size.

cards.title: The Clockwork hero
cards.text: "Influence time." Three takes. Mine: the chronomancer with a pocket watch for a hat.
cards.why: A white dial with two hands is the one clock sign that still reads at game size, so I'd take the watch. The wind-up man's key can turn in the game. Father Time is the weakest: at game size he is an old wizard. The game keeps its stand-in until you pick.

items.label: A the pocket-watch hat
items.text: A chronomancer: a great brass pocket watch worn as a hat, a pendulum staff, a cog turning over the free hand.

items.label: B the wind-up man
items.text: A brass man whose face is a clock (twenty past eight makes a moustache), a key in his back, a clock hand for a sword.

items.label: C Father Time
items.text: A hood, a long white beard, a clock-hand staff, an hourglass hanging from the left fist.

cards.title: The Air mage
cards.text: "Whirled effect." Three takes. Mine: the white hood drawn up into a curl of wind.
cards.why: The curl and the spiral are the whirl, and it sits in the mages' family beside Storm and Frost. The fans would work both hands in turn. The one blown sideways is the weakest: the hair reads as a head wrap. The game keeps its stand-in until you pick.

items.label: A the curl of wind
items.text: A white hood with a spiral on it and a curled tip, a scarf streaming back, a curled staff, a whirlwind over the free hand.

items.label: B the spiral hat and fans
items.text: A wide round hat painted with one spiral, a paper fan in each hand.

items.label: C blown sideways
items.text: No hat: white hair and a scarf blown hard to one side, a pinwheel for a staff.

cards.title: The Warden
cards.text: Shackles, restraints, nullification. Three takes. Mine: the helm made like a padlock.
cards.why: The padlock is a shape nobody else has, and its pale keyhole can carry the nullifying glow. It has no face, like the Tower. The gaoler keeps a face, behind bars. The witch-finder is the weakest: its hat sits near the Witch's. The game keeps its stand-in until you pick.

items.label: A the padlock helm
items.text: A closed helm made like a padlock, a glowing keyhole, the shackle arching over the back, a shackle on a chain in each fist.

items.label: B the gaoler and his key
items.text: A pot helm with a cage of bars over the face, a great key held like a mace, a shackle in the left hand.

items.label: C the witch-finder
items.text: A black hat with a padlock buckle, chains over the shoulders to a padlock under the chin, a man-catcher fork.

cards.title: The Telekinetic
cards.text: Three takes. Mine: fists at the temples, two swords hanging in the air with no hand on them.
cards.why: The swords with no hands on them say what the hero does, and they are the two arm parts, so the game can swing them. The turban's three stones can circle. The blindfold's floating braid is the weakest read. The game keeps its stand-in until you pick.

items.label: A swords that hang in the air
items.text: An indigo hood with an eye gem, both fists at the temples, a sword floating in front of each shoulder, a ring of force round each grip.

items.label: B the turban and the stones
items.text: A white turban with a violet gem, both hands open, three stones hanging in the air behind.

items.label: C blindfold, braid, boulder
items.text: An indigo blindfold, a silver braid floating up behind, a boulder hanging before the open right hand.

cards.title: The Earth mage
cards.text: Quakes, chains of spikes, stone walls. Three takes. Mine: the stone-shaper with rock fists.
cards.why: The rock fists have the strongest outline of all the takes, and pounding the ground is the earthquake. The ring of spikes is the spike spell worn on the back. The stone hood is the weakest: the Frost mage's build in brown. The game keeps its stand-in until you pick.

items.label: A the rock fists
items.text: A boulder for a cap (moss, amber crystals), a russet beard in two braids, each fist in a great glove of rock.

items.label: B the ring of spikes
items.text: A ring of rock spikes round the back of the shoulders, a bun with a stone pin, a carved standing stone for a staff.

items.label: C the stone hood
items.text: A brown hood with a keystone and an amber gem, columns of rock off the shoulders, a boulder staff.

cards.title: Summons and props, drawn
cards.text: The things the game draws in code today, as art: each hero with its own beside it, at game scale.
cards.why: One design each, in the props' style, with the heroes' line weight at their size in the game. None is in the game yet: mark any part that is off and I'll redo it before it goes in.

parts.title: Haymaker: the hay bale
parts.text: A rolled bale with two bands of twine.

parts.title: Shaman: totem and spirits
parts.text: A carved, painted pole like the one on his back; the bear, eagle and beaver in one pale blue style with a swirl on each back.

parts.title: Alchemist: the cauldron
parts.text: A black iron pot, green brew to the brim.

parts.title: Warlock: imp and demon form
parts.text: His own imp in his colours, and his demon form as its own bust with the great sword.

parts.title: Beekeeper: the hive
parts.text: A straw skep on a round board.

parts.title: Quartermaster: crate, barricade
parts.text: A roped crate with the red cross; a wall of pointed planks, and the same with spikes.

parts.title: Crossbowman: the pavise
parts.text: A tall shield in his red and yellow on its prop.

parts.title: Grenadier: the big bomb
parts.text: His bomb, large, with a brass collar and a lit fuse.

parts.title: Engineer: towers and drones
parts.text: The torcher, the tesla tower, the snowball mortar and the medbay on one kind of round wooden deck; the med drone and the wind-up drone.

cards.title: Six heroes' weapon hands
cards.text: Your notes on how they hold things, drawn: each hero as it is now, then the new one. Not in the game yet.
cards.why: Each changes only the hand and what it holds. Mark any part that is off.

parts.title: Bearskin: paws on his hands
parts.text: You wrote: "The bear paws of his outfit should be on his hands. Move with it. I didn't like this club." The paws ride on the arms now; a new club, a gnarled root, is its own part so it can go away when he claws.

parts.title: Warhelm: the hammer by itself
parts.text: The hammer is its own part, so it can leave his hand and float while both fists punch. At rest nothing looks different.

parts.title: Bulwark: further from the tip
parts.text: You wrote: "Holding spear too close to tip." The same spear, slid forward through the fist.

parts.title: Valkyrie: holding the spear
parts.text: You wrote: "Hold spear better." The same spear, held at the shaft across the front, the fist in plain sight.

parts.title: Samurai: both hands
parts.text: You wrote: "Should hold with 2 hands in front of him." The same katana, across the front in both fists.

parts.title: Trapper: shotgun, trap on hip
parts.text: You wrote: "I want them to have a shotgun. Should hold with 2 hands. Trap sits on their back hip." A double-barrelled shotgun in both fists; the trap behind the left shoulder.
